name: The Steamboat Hotel's Stable

documented_range.note: COPIED FROM THE HOUSE IT SERVES (data/structures/steamboat_hotel.json, phase frame_1835, 1835-01-01 to 1835-12-31). No source dates this building, because no source mentions it. The stable is taken to stand while the house kept travellers, because keeping a traveller's horse overnight was a priced service of a Chicago tavern from the county's first licences on (the 1831 order below). If the house kept its horses at a livery or a neighbour's barn instead, this range is wrong in the only way that matters: the building was not there. T-1776.

position.symbolic_location: North-west of (behind) the Steamboat Hotel on the north bank, away from its river and Kinzie Street front.
position.note: NOTHING PLACES THIS BUILDING AND THIS COORDINATE IS A CHOICE, bounded by the lot. The placement policy's ancillary clause (`ancillary_behind_its_own_roof`: stables 'go off the block alley behind the roof they serve') and the house's own footprint decide where it may go; inside that, it is behind the house, on the landward side away from the front it turns south-east toward the landing (bearing 131.4): about 5 m clear of the house's north-west corner, clear of the Council House to the north-east and of the reconstructed houses to the west, off the platted lots, and dry at every corner. The door faces south, toward the house. Checked against every committed footprint with a 1 m clearance and against the modelled water; nothing was hit. L313.

derivation.reason: Placed against the lot it stands on (data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json) or, off the plat, against the house it serves — neither is a street line or a traced waterline that validate.py can re-derive a coordinate from. The reasoning is in position.note.

footprint.note: INVENTED, AND SIZED FROM THE HOUSE'S BEDS. The lodging model (data/reconstruction/1835_lodging_model.json, T-1164) puts 11 in the Steamboat Hotel on an ordinary night (35 crowded), itself graded reconstructed. ONE STALL PER TWO ORDINARY GUESTS: 11 beds / 2 = 6 = 6 stalls. Half, because the summer of 1835's crowd came mostly by lake and many of a town house's guests arrived without a horse; the Western Hotel's 'teams as numerous as were the guests' (chicagology_prefire278) is that house's own sentence about the teamsters' road west and is not carried to a Lake Street house; one range of 6 single standing stalls 5 ft wide and 9 ft deep, a passage behind them and a mangers' run, 20 ft deep in all, plus a 6 ft bay for harness and feed at one end: 6 x 5 + 6 = 36 ft long by 20 ft deep = 10.97 x 6.1 m. The ordinary night, not the crowded one, as the beds are sized. Every factor is ours and stated so it can be replaced: an advertisement or a sale notice naming this house's stabling, a fire-loss list, or a lot-level view of the block. L313.

construction.note: NOT STATED BY ANY SOURCE. Plank, the same reading as the Western Hotel's stable of 1834 and for the same reason: by the time this house kept travellers the town's sawmills of 1832-33 were cutting boards, and a stable is the building a keeper put up quickest and cheapest. The log reading of the Wolf Point stable is the earlier date's answer and is not carried here.

wall_height_m.note: No figure is attested. 3.0 m is about 10 ft: a horse led in under a header with a loft for hay above the stalls, and the archetype's own size-aware default for a footprint of this size. What is inferred is the range, not the number.

door.note: THE PRICED SERVICE IS THE ARGUMENT, as at the Wolf Point stable: a horse kept overnight is a horse led in and out, and the archetype's 'stable' door (1.35 m clear) is the opening that allows it.

door_side.note: NOT ATTESTED. The front, at bearing 180, chosen so the door faces the house it serves. L313.

paint.note: No source describes a finish. An unpainted plank stable behind a painted house is the ordinary reading; nothing states it either way.

phases.change_note: A stable behind the Steamboat Hotel, sized from the beds the lodging model gives the house and placed on its own ground. T-1776.

function.note: A PRICE DOCUMENTS A SERVICE; THE BUILDING IS THE INFERENCE. The Cook County Court of County Commissioners, sitting at Chicago on 13 April 1831, 'Ordered that the following rates be allowed to tavern keepers', among them 'For each horse fed 25' and 'Keeping horse one night 50' (Andreas, scan p. 249). That order set what a licensed Chicago house might charge to keep a traveller's horse; it is read here as standing for every public house the lodging model sizes, which is an inference, because no licence for this house in particular has been read. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE: a dedicated building. A horse can be kept at a picket line, in a fenced lot or at a livery up the street; this record draws the building because a house of this size on a Lake Street lot with an alley behind it is the ordinary case, and says so.

occupants.value: the house's keeper — John Davis, keeper
occupants.note: Taken to have passed with the house (data/structures/steamboat_hotel.json's occupants). No hostler is named and no source attaches any person to this building.

land_owner.value: The ground was entered by Robert A Kenzie, 7 May 1831
land_owner.note: KINZIE'S ADDITION. The north fraction of section 10 is the section north of the river, which is why the register prints 102.29 acres and not a quarter's 160. It is resolved as the section's own grid box clipped to the committed north bank of the main stem (`e1834_harbor_cut/shoreline.geojson`), so no boundary here is authored. The two rows the register carries for it — one plain, one with the school-section marker — are the same entry printed twice. THE REGISTER SPELLS THE PURCHASER MORE THAN ONE WAY for this same tract — Robert A Kenzie; Robert A Kinzie — and the spellings are carried rather than merged, which is the land_sales crosswalk's standing rule: tract agreement is where two spellings MIGHT be one man and is never proof that they are. THE MARGIN IS 63 m: this footprint stands that far inside the tract's nearest boundary, which is more than twice the working horizontal uncertainty of anything traced off the 1834 sheets (about 20 m), so the assignment survives the error the construction carries. WHAT THIS ROW CLAIMS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT. It claims that the tract the Illinois State Archives' land-sale register describes contains this structure's committed position — the patent for this ground was ENTERED by this man on this date. It does not claim he still held the ground on 1 July 1835, that he lived here, or that he ever stood on it: a sale is a transaction, and the register's only column about residence names a county. THE SECTION LINES ARE CONSTRUCTED, NOT TRACED (L219): the grid is carried from the single PLSS corner at State & Madison, on the plat's own east-west bearing, in nominal one-mile squares.

research_note: T-1776, the second piece of T-1209: every licensed house the lodging model sizes read for its horse-keeping against its beds. This is the Steamboat Hotel's reading — 11 ordinary beds, 6 stalls. WHAT WOULD REPLACE IT: any advertisement of the house naming its stabling (the Chicago American and the Democrat of 1834-35 carry the hotels' cards), the 1839 fire-loss lists, or a lot-level reading of Wright 1834 / Hathaway 1834 for this block. docs/RESEARCH/1835_tavern_horse_keeping.md carries the ledger for all nine houses.
